calls.head: Like for like: Barron vs. Duclair
calls.body: At home, the Jets keep sending Barron’s line (Koepke, Barron and Zhilkin) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Scott Arniel keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Islanders’ fourth line is Duclair, Cizikas and Chaffee.

calls.head: Where the Islanders have the edge: depth
calls.body: The Islanders are the league’s best for depth, and the Jets are near the bottom. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Islanders spread their forward ice time deeper down the lineup than the Jets.

surprises.head: Winnipeg’s power play feasted on the Islanders’ kill
surprises.body: The Islanders have one of the league’s leakiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a big night: Winnipeg’s power play created 21.1 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.6 (about 8.2 against the Islanders) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 225 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Morrissey ends it in overtime
paras: The first period was a wild one. Anthony Duclair got the scoring started for the Islanders early in the period, but Morgan Barron tied it up for Winnipeg 31 seconds later. Emil Heineman restored the Islanders’ lead shorthanded midway through the period. Kyle Connor tied it 2-2 for Winnipeg late in the period, and Kyle Palmieri put the Islanders back ahead 3-2 just 20 seconds into the second. Cole Perfetti made it 3-3 for Winnipeg on the power play midway through the period. The Isles’ Ryan Pulock left late in the period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with a lower-body injury. Josh Morrissey won it just under two minutes into overtime. Mark Scheifele finished with three assists.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Daws shook off a shaky start for the Jets, allowing three goals on the first nine shots and none on the last 16, and Semyon Varlamov stopped 18 of 22 at the other end. The Jets moved to 11-9-3, sixth in the Central, while the Islanders fell to 10-6-5, fourth in the Metropolitan.
